label: Precise grotesk
comment: Linear's display discipline (an in-between weight, tracking held as a token) on Wix Madefor's Display and Text cuts.
summary: Linear's display discipline (one in-between weight, tight tracking held as tokens) set on Wix Madefor's separate Display and Text cuts, with JetBrains Mono for commands: exact and quiet, so the offer's numbers carry the page.

refs.name: Linear
refs.what: Display as a house cut: Inter at an in-between 510 weight, -0.022em tracking and 1.0 leading, all tokens, over 15px/1.6 body. This takes the discipline, not the face (Inter as display is the canon's default case), and swaps its commercial Berkeley Mono for JetBrains Mono.

refs.name: Wix Madefor (Dalton Maag)
refs.what: A superfamily drawn as separate Display and Text cuts, the same optical split Linear gets from Inter's display size, so headlines can run tight while 16px text stays open.

tokens.--font-display: 'Wix Madefor Display', 'Wix Madefor Text', system-ui, sans-serif

label: Geist with pixel display
comment: Geist Pixel Square is drawn on a 38/1000 em grid (26.316 pixels per em). Display sizes snap to the nearest multiple of 13.158px, so one pixel is a whole device pixel at DPR 2.
summary: Vercel's family moved one step toward the owner's pixels: Geist Pixel Square sets the headlines on its native grid (sizes snap to whole pixels), while Geist and Geist Mono keep every paragraph, control and command plain; the live site already reads in Geist.

refs.name: Vercel
refs.what: Geist Pixel is drawn on Geist's metrics and vercel.com loads Geist, Geist Mono and five Geist Pixel cuts together. This keeps Vercel's pairing and gives the pixel cut the one display job.

refs.name: Omarchy
refs.what: Pixels stay in the display layer (its pixel logotype) while reading text stays in Geist and a real mono. Here the pixel face is likewise never body, label or control text.

refs.name: pi
refs.what: One pixel element as the brand moment above calm reading text, never pixel paragraphs.

license: OFL-1.1: Geist, Geist Mono and Geist Pixel Square (Vercel). Latin subsets, unhinted; OFL texts in fonts/.

label: Light ledger
comment: Mona Sans and Source Code Pro reserve their names ('Mona', 'Source'), so these instanced Latin subsets are renamed inside the font and in CSS, as the OFL requires of modified versions.
summary: Stripe's register in OFL faces: an Akzidenz-rooted grotesk (Mona Sans, renamed in the subset) set light, 300 for headlines and 350 for reading, with Source Code Pro for code; calm and expensive, and easy to read about money.

refs.name: Stripe
refs.what: Söhne at weight 300 for display and body alike, with Source Code Pro Medium for code (stripe.com CSS, 2026-10-29). Söhne is commercial, so the light grotesk here is Mona Sans, which shares its Akzidenz-Grotesk ancestry; body sits at 350 so it stays readable on the dark theme.

refs.name: Mona Sans (GitHub)
refs.what: An OFL grotesk drawn from industrial-era grotesques; at weight 300 its joins stay crisp at 84px, which is what makes a light headline look deliberate rather than faint.

license: OFL-1.1: Mona Sans (GitHub) and Source Code Pro (Adobe). Both reserve their names ('Mona', 'Source'), so these modified Latin subsets are renamed Misty Ledger Sans and Misty Ledger Code; OFL texts in fonts/.

label: Book italic
comment: The Brygada italic file is registered as its own family in normal style, so --font-display alone turns headlines italic without another layer setting font-style.
summary: pi and Earendil's book voice: Brygada 1918 italic for headlines, its roman for 19px reading text and controls, and Commit Mono for commands, so a software studio reads like a well-set book.

refs.name: pi
refs.what: Plantin italic for h1 and h2, roman Plantin for 22px reading text, Commit Mono for commands. Plantin is commercial; Brygada 1918 is the OFL old-style serif nearest its sturdy, large-x-height texture, and Commit Mono is used as pi uses it.

refs.name: Earendil
refs.what: One italic statement carries the page while everything around it stays quiet; the italic is the voice, not decoration on every heading.

refs.name: Brygada 1918
refs.what: A revival of a 1918 Polish Garalde whose italic keeps its calligraphic warmth at 84px and whose roman stays even at 19px.

label: Mono console
comment: Martian Mono is instanced twice from one variable file: width 87.5 for headlines, width 100 for controls and code.
summary: A developer system where mono is the declared material: Martian Mono in a narrow cut for headlines and at regular width for controls and code, with Host Grotesk for every paragraph; it fits stack.mistystep.io, where commands are the product.

refs.name: Greptile
refs.what: Mono as the product's own material: nav, links and labels in Space Mono beside a heavy display face and a plain sans for sentences. Here mono moves up into the headline and the controls, and paragraphs stay in a grotesk.

refs.name: Macroscope
refs.what: Geist Mono beside Geist for an AI code reviewer: mono reads as the code tool's voice without ever setting a paragraph.

refs.name: Martian Mono (Evil Martians)

label: Industrial condensed
comment: Display runs in capitals through --display-transform; reading text and controls never do.
summary: Brass Hands' industrial register: Sofia Sans Extra Condensed in capitals for headlines, Sofia Sans for reading and controls, and Kode Mono for code; loud at the top, plain everywhere else.

refs.name: Brass Hands
refs.what: Status-plate type: brasshands.com sets every visible line in one square mono (Construct Mono, commercial, by Marius Roosendaal) beside a condensed wordmark, and its client systems pair display capitals with mono spec tables. Here Sofia Sans Extra Condensed carries the capitals and Kode Mono the square technical voice, both under the OFL.

refs.name: Grok
refs.what: grok.com runs one grotesk family in Text and Display cuts (Universal Sans, commercial) for every word, keeps monos (IBM Plex Mono, Geist Mono) for code, and uses five sizes on its home page. Here Sofia Sans plays both cuts (Extra Condensed for display, regular width for reading) and Kode Mono is only for code.

label: Steps (C)
comment: Round C's type, ported. Bitcount Grid Single (element shape 50: solid square pixels) covers only the digits and '/' inside the display family, so large figures set in --font-display turn pixel while letters stay Archivo. Its face repeats the Archivo display face's descriptors and comes last, so browsers merge the two by unicode-range.
summary: Round C's type, ported: Archivo wide and heavy for display and at normal width for reading, Fragment Mono for code, and Bitcount pixel numerals inside the display stack so large figures turn pixel.

refs.name: Omarchy
refs.what: Pixels on one strict grid as a material. C kept pixels to numerals only, never running text or labels.

refs.name: Bitcount (TYPETR)
refs.what: Petr van Blokland's grid numerals: one element is 0.1em, so they are crisp at 40 and 80px, the sizes C used.

refs.name: Archivo (Omnibus-Type)
refs.what: A width axis: wide and heavy (112, 740) for display, normal width for reading, one family for a direction built on a unit.
